text:
Shea Theodore has 5 points in 18 games, which looks like a slow start until you see what Vegas does with him on the ice. The Golden Knights take almost 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he plays, nearly ten points better than without him. That's a big gap for a defenseman who plays 22 minutes.

The points are what's missing. His rate of 0.76 per 60 minutes is below the range we'd expect (1.0 to 1.5), and Vegas has scored about 2.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. He has zero hits all season, which says something about his style, and 23 blocked shots, which says he's doing the other work.

Evolving-Hockey had him 46th among 215 defensemen last season, with an adjusted impact on chance creation in the 87th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a less obvious skill: he stops 15% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. He's 31, a Cup winner in 2023, and plays 22 minutes a night. We project about 35 points. When the bounces even out, they'll come in bunches.
headline: Theodore drives it, the points lag
